newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ's Tower Group reports "huge growth" in 1996.
newsitem.headline: NZ's Tower Group reports "huge growth" in 1996.

text.p: Tower Financial Services said on Wednesday it had increased its statutory reserves (retained earnings) by NZ$49 million in 1996, bringing its solvency level up to 23 percent.
Group managing director James Boonzaier said total revenue was up by over 50 percent to NZ$2.1 billion.
"More importantly, premiums, contributions and subscriptions are up 35 percent to $973 million," he said.
"By the same token, management expenses rose only by seven percent to $232 million, signalling another year of productivity improvement of between 10 and 20 percent across the group."
Gross returns on managed funds in 1996 had been in a range of 10 to 12 percent in New Zealand and 11 to 13 percent in Australia.
The full year after-tax increase in group funds under management was $981 million (before allowing for an extraordinary increase of $2.0 billion from the Austrust acquisition).
This exceeded Tower's planned increase of $766 million and reflected strong inflows from new investors, particularly wholesale investors in New Zealand and retail investors in Australia.
Boonzaier said that with AMP's recent announcement that it would demutualise, it was the only remaining Australasian Mutual which had not made an announcement in this regard.
"The company has however indicated that the matter is under review by the board," he said.
Companies in the Tower Group include Tower Life Australia, National Insurance, Trustees Executors and Austrust.
